newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent sideways after U.S. gasoline stems losse.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent sideways after U.S. gasoline stems losse.

text.p: IPE Brent futures maintained modest losses, recovering most of a larger earlier fall, helped by U.S. gasoline.
February Brent at 1835 GMT was trading down 16 cents at $23.73 a barrel, up from its $23.52 session low.
January gas oil ended down 50 cents at $222 and lost $1.25 versus February as players rolled long positions forward.
News of the shutdown of a gasoline catalytic cracking unit at Exxon's Baton Rouge refinery in Louisiana helped prices off their lows after some profit-taking from Monday's big rise.
"People generally were expecting the market to come off even further because technically it was looking overbought but the Exxon news prevented a second break lower," said a broker in London.
Dealers in London remained cautious ahead of tonight's release of latest weekly U.S. inventory statistics.
Last week's prices fell after the American Petroleum Institute reported at 2.11 million barrel build in middle distillates.
Cold weather forecast later this week for the U.S. northeast has helped drive prices back up with Brent gaining more than a dollar on Monday.
